label: Liquid Tiles
title: Liquid Tile API
lead: Register swimmable world liquids with custom visuals, touch effects, drinking behavior, and worldgen.
bodyHtml:
Liquids? Tiles? Why not combine the two?

LiquidTileRegistry is CUCoreLib's world-liquid API. It registers custom fluid cells in the vanilla FluidManager, gives them a stable custom world byte, and patches the normal liquid systems so they can render, be drunk, fill containers, and affect bodies standing in them.

This is different from Liquid API. A liquid registration defines what a logical liquid is. A liquid tile registration defines how that liquid behaves when it exists as a pool in the world.

LiquidRegistry.Register("acidbrine", new CustomLiquidInfo
{
    name = "Acid brine",
    description = "A shimmering pool of caustic industrial runoff.",
    color = new Color(0.72f, 0.96f, 0.28f),
    valuePerLiter = 8f,
    onDrink = (ml, body) =>
    {
        float dose = ml * 0.01f;
        body.Drink(dose * 2f);
        body.sicknessAmount += dose * 9f;
        body.happiness -= dose * 3f;
    }
});

LiquidTileRegistry.Register("acidbrinepool", new CustomLiquidTileInfo
{
    LiquidId = "acidbrine",
    FillLiquidId = "acidbrine",
    Tint = new Color(0.8f, 1f, 0.45f, 1f),
    TemperaturePerSecond = 4f,
    SicknessPerSecond = 6f,
    WetnessPerSecond = 30f,
    SlipPerSecond = 0.35f,
    SpawnAmount = 0.15f
});

What gets patched for you

Once registered, CUCoreLib hooks the tile into the normal game liquid flow. FluidManager.WaterInfo reads your buoyancy and drag, LiquidColor and LiquidName use your registered display data, DrinkLiquid can consume the pool through the linked liquid, and Body.HandleVariableUpdates applies touch effects every frame.

That means you do not need a separate Harmony patch just to make a custom swamp, acid pond, algae bath, or healing puddle act like a real world liquid.

CustomLiquidTileInfo

CustomLiquidTileInfo controls the world-facing behavior of the liquid tile. Most mods only need to set the linked liquid IDs, visuals, touch effects, and maybe worldgen.

FieldTypeWhat it does
LiquidIdstringLogical liquid used for display color fallback, drinking, and tooltip locale lookup. Defaults to the tile registration ID.
FillLiquidIdstringLiquid ID loose containers receive when they fill from this tile. Defaults to LiquidId.
BuoyancyfloatReturned through FluidManager.WaterInfo so bodies float or sink differently in this liquid.
DragfloatMovement resistance used while inside the liquid.
PushBodiesboolIf true, CUCoreLib marks the body as inWater while touching the tile.
WetnessPerSecondfloatWetness added to the body each second.
TemperaturePerSecondfloatTemperature change applied every second while touching the tile.
SicknessPerSecondfloatSickness buildup per second.
DirtynessPerSecondfloatDirtyness added per second.
DisinfectPerSecondfloatRefreshes limb disinfect time while standing in the liquid.
SlipPerSecondfloatAdds to body.liquidSlipTime for slippery liquids.
RagdollBarDrainPerSecondfloatSubtracts from body.liquidRagdollBar over time.
ConsumeOnDrinkboolIf true, drinking removes the world liquid cell after use.
ConsumeOnFillboolWhether filling containers should consume the world liquid tile through the game's normal fill flow.
OnDrinkOverrideLiquidType.OnDrinkOptional direct drink callback for the tile. If unset, the linked LiquidId onDrink is used instead.
OnEnterAction<Body, LiquidTileTouchContext>Called once when a body steps into this liquid tile.
OnTouchAction<Body, LiquidTileTouchContext>Called every frame while a body remains on the tile, after the built-in wetness/sickness/slip effects.
OnExitAction<Body, LiquidTileTouchContext>Called once when a body leaves the tile.

Visuals

Custom liquid tiles keep using the game's fluid rendering path. For a custom surface, set Texture to your PNG and use Opacity for translucency:

LiquidTileRegistry.Register("acidbrinepool", new CustomLiquidTileInfo
{
    LiquidId = "acidbrine",
    FillLiquidId = "acidbrine",
    Texture = "Images.acidbrine-surface.png",
    Opacity = 0.7f,
    Tint = Color.white
});

Texture accepts an embedded resource in the registering assembly, or a loose file with an absolute path or a path relative to that assembly's directory. The two-argument Register(id, info) captures the caller assembly. Wrapper libraries can use Register(id, info, Assembly sourceAssembly) to select the assembly that owns the texture.

When the texture loads successfully, it takes precedence over VisualMode and VisualMaterial. CUCoreLib automatically clones the game's magma material, binds your image to _MagmaTex, and sets _EmmisTex to black so the pool respects room lighting. Filtering is always bilinear with repeat wrapping. Particle quads fit one cell while keeping the shorter surface row.

The PNG must already tile seamlessly, preferably with fully opaque pixels: it repeats once per world cell. CUCoreLib does not generate or validate seams, and there is no seamless toggle. For this texture path only, rendered alpha is the logical liquid color's alpha × Tint.a × Opacity; opacity defaults to 0.7f and is clamped to 0–1.

Local texture assets are not transmitted in multiplayer. Every peer needs the same texture installed.

FieldTypeWhat it does
TexturestringSeamlessly tiling PNG resource or file path. A successful load overrides the visual mode/material with a room-lit magma material clone.
OpacityfloatTexture-path alpha multiplier on logical liquid color alpha × Tint.a. Defaults to 0.7; clamped to 0–1. Does not affect other visual paths.
VisualModeLiquidTileVisualModeChooses whether the tile reuses an existing vanilla fluid visual, a custom material, a sprite texture, or a generated high-res image when no texture loads.
ExistingVisualLiquidBytebyteBase vanilla liquid visual to clone from. Defaults to 1 which is water.
TintColorMultiplier applied to the linked liquid color for fluid rendering and tile tooltip color.
VisualMaterialMaterialManual or imported material override used when VisualMode is Material and no texture loads.
VisualSpriteSpriteSprite texture override used when VisualMode is Sprite. It still reuses the current fluid material.
HighResImageTexture2DTexture override used when VisualMode is HighResImageGenerated. It still reuses the current fluid material.

Without Texture, existing manual/imported materials, sprite, high-res image, and tint behavior are unchanged. Use ExistingLiquidPlusTint for a recolored vanilla liquid, Texture for a custom room-lit surface, or VisualMaterial for a custom shader path.

Placement and worldgen

Use LiquidTileRegistry.Place(id, blockPos) to place one custom liquid cell into an empty world block, or FloodFill(id, start, maxFill) to spread the liquid outward using the vanilla fill simulation.

For terrain generation, set SpawnAmount above 0f. CUCoreLib patches WorldGeneration.GenerateOres() and calls world.PlaceLiquids(...) for each registered tile that matches the current biome layer mask.

FieldTypeWhat it does
SpawnAmountfloatHow often the liquid generates during world creation. Values above 0f opt into generation.
SpawnLayersintLayer mask controlling which biome depths can spawn this liquid. Use LiquidTileRegistry.AllSpawnLayersMask for every layer, or the same helper-mask pattern as tiles/buildings when you need specific layers.
MaxFloodFillintDefault maximum fill size for FloodFill and worldgen placement.

Touch callbacks

The callback context reports the block position, world position, custom world byte, delta time, and whether the body just entered or exited. Use it for special logic that should happen on top of the built-in wetness, sickness, disinfect, or slip behavior.

LiquidTileRegistry.Register("healingpool", new CustomLiquidTileInfo
{
    LiquidId = "disinfectant",
    WetnessPerSecond = 8f,
    DisinfectPerSecond = 20f,
    OnEnter = (body, context) =>
    {
        body.talker.Say("Warm...");
    },
    OnTouch = (body, context) =>
    {
        if (body.health < 100f)
            body.health += 2f * context.DeltaTime;
    },
    OnExit = (body, context) =>
    {
        body.happiness += 1f;
    }
});

Persistence and multiplayer

Liquid tile definitions, their world-byte mapping, and current custom-liquid cells are already included in CUCoreLib's built-in save and multiplayer snapshot flow. The registry registers a world save provider during startup, and the multiplayer sync registry includes a dedicated liquidtiles module.

The one important caveat is content reload: strict replayable content reload does not support liquid tile registration right now, so LiquidTileRegistry.Register() intentionally rejects that path.
